newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT -Grace Q4 earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT -Grace Q4 earnings forecast.

text.p: W.R. Grace and Co issued the following statement on its fourth quarter results.
-- Grace said earnings and sales would be less than expected in Q4.
-- Operating earnings will be in mid 60 cent range for Q4.
-- Full year earnings per share will be up about 15 percent.
-- Grace expects Q4 charges from litigation, restructuring, asset impairments.
-- Grace said it is in the final stages of bidding for sale of its cocoa, polymers units.
A full text of the company's statement follows.
Grace Announces Fourth Quarter Estimate

BOCA RATON, Fla., Dec. 19 /PRNewswire/ -- W. R. Grace & Co. (NYSE: GRA) announced today that each of its three core businesses is expected to achieve record sales in the fourth quarter. Total Grace sales are expected to increase approximately seven percent over the prior year quarter. However, the recognition in the fourth quarter of expected future operating losses in the to-be-divested TEC Systems air emissions control business is expected to result in operating earnings per share in the mid-60 cent range.

Excluding anticipated fourth quarter losses and the accrual of 1997 estimated operating losses for TEC Systems through its planned sale in 1997, the company expects fourth quarter operating earnings per share to be in the mid to high 70 cent range, compared to 63 cents in the fourth quarter of 1995. On this basis, EPS for the full year is expected to increase approximately 15 percent. The fourth quarter and full year 1995 included six cents per share from the favorable settlement of prior years' tax returns.

The company expects sales and earnings growth in the quarter to be less than previously anticipated due to continued weakness in some of its packaging and catalyst markets. Sales and earnings from the company's flexible plastic packaging business continue to be impacted by market conditions for fresh red meat in North America and display films globally, as well as a continuation of the Mad Cow disease issue in Europe. Competitive pricing and pressure on refining margins continue to impact Grace's fluid cracking catalyst business.
The company said it is continuing to take steps to achieve earnings in 1997 within the range of analyst expectations.

"Despite lower than expected sales, we have maintained our overall market positions," said Albert J. Costello, Grace chairman, president and chief executive officer. "Given our strong market leadership, the continued penetration of our new products and an intensified effort to reduce operating expenses company-wide, we remain confident that we will deliver significantly higher earnings in 1997 -- even if our sales growth continues at the same pace we are experiencing in the fourth quarter of 1996."
Actions taken in 1996 to decrease operating expenses include:
-- Continuing manufacturing cost reductions in all three core businesses
-- Cost reductions in the European packaging organization
-- The elimination of the corporate research organization
-- Reduction of the number of corporate officers
-- Restructuring of marketing and sales organizations
-- Consolidation of support services

Costello said that Grace should see substantial positive free operating cash flow in 1997 as a result of reduced capital spending and continuing focus on improved working capital management, as well as higher earnings. He also indicated that the company expects to complete its 20 percent share repurchase program in the first quarter of 1997. Since launching this program, Grace has repurchased more than 11 million shares. This is in addition to ten million shares purchased prior to the NMC transaction in September.
The company expects to record special charges in the fourth quarter related to several matters, including asbestos bodily injury litigation and claims, restructuring activities and asset impairments.

In October, Grace announced that it plans to divest four non-core businesses, including TEC Systems. It had been in discussions with one interested buyer for the sale of TEC, but has terminated those discussions. A competitive bidding process for the two primary segments of TEC Systems is planned for early 1997.

Divestiture of the other three businesses remains on schedule. The company announced in November an agreement to sell its Amicon business to Millipore Corp. for $125 million and expects to complete the transaction in January 1997. Grace is in final stages of the competitive bidding process to sell its cocoa and specialty polymers businesses and expects to name buyers by early 1997.
Grace is a leading global supplier of flexible packaging and specialty chemicals with annual sales of approximately $3.3 billion. The company operates in more than 100 countries.
